findings.title: updateCredential return value used ambiguously to detect userStorage success
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential relies on user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) returning true to mean 'created in user storage'. However updateCredential's contract is generic (used for updating any credential type) and some storage providers may return true for reasons unrelated to actually persisting a new recovery-codes credential (e.g. no-op success), or false even though partially processed. This mirrors the same questionable pattern already used for OTP but duplicates the ambiguity for a new credential type without additional safety checks (e.g. verifying supportsCredentialType first), risking silently creating duplicate or no credential in edge-case federated providers.

findings.title: Missing null checks on required form parameters before use
findings.body: generatedCodesString, generatedAtTimeString, and generatedUserLabel are read from form parameters without null checks before being used in generatedAtTimeString.equals(...) and Long.valueOf(generatedAtTimeString). If an attacker/misbehaving client submits the required action without these hidden fields, this throws NPE/NumberFormatException instead of being handled gracefully, which existed before but is still unaddressed by this change that otherwise reworks the flow.

findings.title: getCredentials does not use JsonSerialization generics safely
findings.body: JsonSerialization.readValue(myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData(), List.class) uses a raw List type (unchecked generic cast), risking a ClassCastException at runtime if the stored JSON isn't a List<String>, and losing compile-time type safety. This is minor but inconsistent with the typed usage pattern used elsewhere (e.g., CredentialHelper uses List<String> directly).

findings.title: New test only covers single recovery code usage, not exhaustion/removal flow
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only validates login with the first recovery code (index 0) stored in the federated/user-storage provider. It does not test the removeStoredCredentialById or RequiredAction re-trigger path from RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator when allCodesUsed() is true for a user-storage-backed credential, which is directly relevant to the PR's goal of supporting recovery codes in user storage and could hide bugs in that specific interaction (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById may not be supported for federated storage credentials).
